title: Our Lady of the Rosary (7 October)
hook: October is the month of the rosary

segments.voice: Yesterday, Saint Francis and his song of the creatures. Your line was brother sun. Did you greet it? Day six hundred eighty-four.

Look at the rearview mirror of a taxi in Manila or Mexico City, or in the coat pocket of an old man on a bus in Kraków, and there's a decent chance you'll find a string of beads with a small cross at the end. Some people use it every day. Some carry it and haven't prayed it in years. Some were handed one at a funeral and kept it in a drawer. The rosary is maybe the most familiar Catholic object there is. On the seventh of October the Church keeps a feast in its name, and the whole month belongs to it.
screen: `BEADS ON A REARVIEW MIRROR.` → `IN A POCKET, IN A DRAWER.` → `A FEAST, AND A MONTH.`

segments.voice: The word rosary comes from the Latin rosarium, a rose garden. In the Middle Ages, a garland of prayers was pictured as a crown of roses offered to Mary. The shape grew out of the psalms. Monks prayed all hundred and fifty psalms; lay people who couldn't read began praying a hundred and fifty Hail Marys or Our Fathers instead, counted on beads or knots. It was sometimes called Mary's psalter. A popular story says Mary gave the rosary to Saint Dominic. Historians find the rosary taking shape gradually over the centuries instead, and the Dominicans did a great deal to spread it. Then the feast. On the seventh of October, 1571, a fleet gathered by Pope Pius V met the Ottoman navy at Lepanto, off the coast of Greece. Pius had asked Christians to pray the rosary. When word came of the victory, he set up a feast of Our Lady of Victory; his successor renamed it Our Lady of the Rosary. In the 1880s Pope Leo XIII wrote letter after letter about the rosary and gave it the whole month of October. The prayer itself is simple: five decades, each an Our Father, ten Hail Marys and a Glory Be, while you think through a mystery from the lives of Jesus and Mary. Joyful, sorrowful, glorious, and in 2002 John Paul II added the luminous mysteries, from Jesus's public life. The beads keep count so the mind can go somewhere else: to Bethlehem, to the garden, to the empty tomb.
screen: `ROSARIUM: A ROSE GARDEN.` · `150 HAIL MARYS FOR 150 PSALMS.` · `LEPANTO, 7 OCTOBER 1571.` · `FIVE DECADES, FOUR SETS OF MYSTERIES.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: plan five decades this week. Today, pray one, or just begin. If you have beads, hold them. If not, use your ten fingers. Choose one scene to think about: a birth in a stable, perhaps, or the empty tomb. If you pray, pray an Our Father and as many Hail Marys as the bell allows, keeping the scene in mind. If you don't, simply move from finger to finger, one breath each, picturing the scene. Then pick four more days this week. The bell holds the time.
Our Lady of the Rosary. The feast of the seventh of October, begun after Lepanto in 1571; the whole month of October is given to the rosary. Today's word.
screen: `OUR LADY OF THE ROSARY — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: the month of beads. Today, put a rosary, or any string of beads, somewhere you'll see it, in a pocket, by the bed, on the mirror. Day six hundred eighty-four.

howItsDone: Catholics keep the memorial of Our Lady of the Rosary on 7 October and dedicate October to the rosary; many pray it daily that month, alone, as families, or in parish groups, meditating on the joyful, sorrowful, glorious and luminous mysteries.

fork.setup: it's 1571. a fleet is sailing toward a great sea battle. you're Pope Pius V in Rome. what do you ask Christians to do?
fork.reveal: he asked for the rosary. after the victory at Lepanto on 7 October he set up the feast that became Our Lady of the Rosary.
